headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared file-based workflows; Plandex’s write-capable sandbox can also conflict with next-ai-draw-io’s document-processing outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and diagram XML and uses MCP/browser-based workflows, while Plandex reads and writes a project directory with review-then-apply. If next-ai-draw-io’s generated content is placed into Plandex inputs, instruction-like text can be treated as trusted content. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from documented file-based interaction.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io output is copied into a Plandex plan or project file without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled on content produced by next-ai-draw-io, malicious instructions can be executed.
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Manually strip instructions from imported documents.
Use a separate staging folder for next-ai-draw-io outputs.
Review any generated plan before apply.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch local files, and next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text, images, and diagram XML while also calling external model APIs. Plandex reads and writes the project directory and sends context to a model provider. If the same workspace contains sensitive documents, content can flow from A into B and then to third-party inference. The shared-workspace pathway is documented enough to warrant medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, sensitive files can be exposed to both.
IF next-ai-draw-io forwards document contents to external APIs, those contents can leave the local environment.
IF Plandex is pointed at the same workspace, its model-provider calls can transmit file contents externally.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Exclude secrets and regulated documents from the shared directory.
Disable external model calls for sensitive runs.
Redact documents before importing them into next-ai-draw-io.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem and modify git state, while next-ai-draw-io can run browsers, use MCP, and process files. If both are pointed at the same repo or directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. Because Plandex explicitly supports multiple instances and shared state, the conflict pathway is credible in default multi-agent use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF Plandex modifies git state while next-ai-draw-io edits diagram files in the same tree, conflicts can corrupt work.
IF multiple Plandex instances are active, shared backend state can amplify race conditions.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit or snapshot before running either agent.
Avoid concurrent Plandex instances on the same repo.
Use git locks or a single-writer workflow.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations and document transformations, and Plandex is a planner that can apply changes from its plan-local sandbox. If Plandex consumes next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative, an upstream hallucination or malformed diagram can cascade into incorrect code or repo changes. The review-then-apply design reduces but does not eliminate this risk.
conditions: IF Plandex imports next-ai-draw-io output without verification, errors can propagate into applied changes.
IF next-ai-draw-io generates incorrect diagram XML or text, Plandex may plan against false premises.
IF auto-apply is enabled, the cascade can reach the filesystem without a human check.
mitigations: Require human review before apply.
Validate imported outputs against source documents.
Keep next-ai-draw-io outputs as drafts only.
Turn off auto-apply for cross-agent workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles documents and sends content to multiple external model providers, while Plandex also sends context to a model provider and stores project files in a sandbox. If regulated documents or EU PII are processed, both agents can move the same data into third-party services with different retention and residency terms. No specific certifications are documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io, external model calls may create residency or retention issues.
IF Plandex is used on the same regulated files, its model-provider calls can duplicate the compliance exposure.
IF the operator lacks a DPA or approved provider list, policy violations become plausible.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-regulated data.
Use approved providers only.
Disable cloud inference for sensitive documents.
Document retention and residency settings before use.
